name: ecommerce
description: Meaning and grain problems over the malloy-samples ecommerce package. Goldens are computed from semantics-free truth sources (truth/), never from the semantic model under test.

notes.sizing: 49 cases, 35 dev / 14 holdout. Refusal is measured in both directions: 4 cases where the data is absent and declining is the pass, and 4 that sound like those and are answerable, where declining is the failure. Measuring only the first rewards an agent that refuses everything.
notes.contamination: Lives at the repo root, deliberately outside ecommerce/, which the Publisher serves in full - publisher.json declares no file scoping, so anything under ecommerce/ is indexed and retrievable.
notes.coverage: Coverage per videoamp-eval-framework.md 3.3: 24 covered, 21 derivable, 4 absent. Only absent makes a refusal correct. coverageNote on each non-covered case names the entity that would close it. Re-audited against the model as shipped: three cases moved derivable -> covered because their notes called a measure missing that the model declares (order_items.avg_days_to_ship, storefront.margin_rate), and three notes were corrected without moving a label. A note asserting absence is a claim about one model version and goes stale the moment the model gains a measure; re-audit with check_coverage.py --compare-labels, which prints label-versus-model disagreements and takes no position on which side is wrong. Coverage now 22 covered, 23 derivable, 4 absent: ecom_unsold_inventory and ecom_unsold_stock_value moved covered -> derivable at datasetVersion 15. That settles the OPEN item recorded at version 14, and the modelQuery was the stale side, not the label's premise. Measured: inventory_items declares only `join_one: product with product_id` and nothing joins it to order_items in either direction (ecommerce/ecommerce.malloy), so the PREFERRED 226,427 cannot be reached without writing the relationship inline, which is what derivable means. The goldens themselves were never in doubt: both re-derive exactly from ecommerce-truth. Their modelQuery returns the divergent 216,917 because `sold_at is null` counts the 9,510 cancelled-line items as sold, which is the trap these cases exist to measure -- so for these two the set-wide 'modelQuery reproduces the golden' invariant does not hold, deliberately.
notes.intentCoverage: Coverage judged against ecommerce @ malloy-samples, judged 2026-08-30: 37 of 48 valid intents covered (77%), 6 derivable, 5 absent. Re-judge when the model changes; the rows do not change. Coverage is the ceiling on recall, so recall and precision are computed over the covered set only -- scoring a derivable or absent intent as a retrieval miss blames search for a modelling gap.
notes.retrieval: All 45 answerable cases carry expectedEntities derived from an executing modelQuery that must reproduce the golden. 34 distinct entities exercised. Recall over `required`, precision over anything outside `acceptable`. See RETRIEVAL-SCORING.md.
notes.goldenStatus: All 49 goldens are status: verified as of datasetVersion 15. They were authored and re-derived against ecommerce-truth in August and had been left provisional ever since, which meant nothing scored them: skill:eval-answer issues verdict: null on a provisional golden. Re-measured 2026-09-09 with the shared verifier against an isolated truth Publisher -- verify_goldens.py --set evals/ecommerce --model ecommerce/ecommerce.malloy --publisher <truth> -- which re-derived 45 of 45 answerable goldens exactly and skipped the 4 unanswerable ones, whose pass is a refusal and which need no derivation. Exit 0. A future repair returns the repaired case to provisional until it is re-derived.
